chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The weaver was mentioned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) as being accursed, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is only the one who weaves the lie upon Allah and upon His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.الْحَائِكُ: The weaver (specifically one who weaves lies)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'ha'ik' (weaver) mean in the context of fabricating lies about God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the title 'accursed weaver' (al-ha'ik) refers not to a literal cloth weaver, but to one who 'weaves' or fabricates lies and attributes them to Allah and the Prophet (peace be upon him). This highlights the ethical and theological importance of honesty in religious narration. In Shia hadith sciences, this distinction underscores the gravity of *al-kadhib* (lying) in *riwayah* (narration), where fabricating hadith is considered a major sin that distorts the divine message.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>,

‘The weaver mentioned to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, that he is an accursed one’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather that is the one who weaves the lie upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and upon His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from certain individuals of his people in a marfu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“It was mentioned before abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) that the weaver (knitting) is condemned. The Imam said, ‘It is the one who weaves and fabricates lies against Allah and the Messenger of Allah.”’
